structure: Part 3 read in full the three row-action features under src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/journeys/linear/features/: dashboard (page.js, controller.js, template.njk, notification-helper.js, copy.en.js, copy.cy.js, view-model/sort-options.js, view-model/row/index.js, view-model/row/actions.js, dashboard.fit.spec.js), delete-notification (controller.js, template.njk, copy.en.js, copy.cy.js, delete-notification.fit.spec.js) and cancel-amend (controller.js, template.njk, copy.en.js, copy.cy.js, cancel-amend.fit.spec.js). To resolve what those files reference it also looked up, without claiming their other content, the route helpers in src/server/app/shared/paths.js, the status tag map and CYA_SLUG in src/server/app/shared/kit.js, and the notificationActions and journeyStrip keys in src/server/app/shared/copy.en.js. Covered: the dashboard page (route at the set base, heading, intro, hidden guidance link, start button, Your notifications heading, reference filter, sort select with four options and default, results-range label, one summary card per notification with seven rows, status tags and the Late tag, empty state, previous/next pagination, delete success banner), the start (POST /notifications) and amend (POST /notifications/{journeyId}/amend) actions, the row actions per status (Draft: Resume, Delete; Submitted: View, Amend, Delete; Amending: Resume, Cancel amendment, Delete; no Copy as new), the delete confirmation page (/notifications/{journeyId}/delete) and the cancel amendment page (/notifications/{journeyId}/cancel-amend) with their copy in English and Welsh, guards, outcomes and error handling, and every test in the three fit specs (14 dashboard, 4 delete, 3 cancel-amend).

claims.statement: The dashboard is served by a GET route at the root of the high-risk plants set (the set base path).
The dashboard page's id is 'dashboard' and its slug is empty.
The dashboard's page title and level-1 heading is 'Import notification service'.
The dashboard heading in Welsh is 'Gwasanaeth hysbysu mewnforio'.
A section caption (styled govuk-caption-xl) renders above the dashboard heading when a caption is supplied.
claims.note: The controller does not pass a caption itself; whether one arrives depends on kit.base, outside this part.

claims.statement: The dashboard has a green GOV.UK start button 'Start a new notification', in its own form posting to /notifications with a CSRF crumb.

Starting a notification creates a new journey, begins its linear opening run and redirects to the commodity type page, the first question.
Below the start button the dashboard shows a level-2 heading 'Your notifications' (Welsh 'Eich hysbysiadau').
The notifications area is laid out with the filter in a left one-third column and the results, sort and cards in a right two-thirds column.
The filter panel has a level-3 heading 'Filter notifications' (Welsh 'Hidlo hysbysiadau').
The filter has one text input named referenceNumber labelled 'Keyword or reference' (Welsh 'Allweddair neu gyfeirnod'), prefilled with the current search term.
The filter submits by GET to the dashboard with a 'Search' button (Welsh 'Chwilio') and carries the current sort as a hidden field.
Although labelled 'Keyword or reference', the filter is passed to the list as a reference number; no other keyword matching is visible in the dashboard.
claims.note: How the list call matches the term (exact or partial, reference only or other fields) is in the engine, outside this part.

claims.statement: A search term is trimmed, and a blank or whitespace-only term means no filter.
claims.quote:

claims.statement: The default sort is arrival date newest first, and any unrecognised sort value falls back to it.
The chosen sort option is shown as selected in the sort select.
The dashboard reads page, sort, referenceNumber and deleted from the query string.
A page number that is missing, not a whole number or below 1 is treated as page 1.
A page number beyond the last page is clamped to the last page and the list is fetched again for that page.

claims.statement: The dashboard lists only the signed-in user's own known notifications, fetched page by page from the journey store with the sort and reference filter applied server side.
claims.note: 'Known journeys' scoping is implemented in the engine, outside this part; the empty-state copy says 'in this session'.

claims.statement: Deleted notifications are filtered out of the dashboard list.
Filtering deleted rows after paging means a page can show fewer cards than the page size while the total still counts deleted rows.
claims.note: Only if the backend returns deleted rows; whether it does is outside this part.

A card's reference is the notification reference, falling back to the journey id when no reference has been issued.
Each card shows seven rows in this order: Commodity, Origin, Arrival, Consignor, Status, Date created, Date submitted.

claims.statement: The copy keeps a 'Reference' key (Welsh 'Cyfeirnod') that the card does not render as a row; the reference is the card title instead.
The copy keeps a 'Not submitted' string (Welsh 'Heb ei gyflwyno') that nothing in the dashboard renders; an unsubmitted card's Date submitted row is empty instead.
The Commodity row shows the commodity's name, or failing that its text, category or genus, or a plain string commodity as-is, or blank.
The Origin row shows the country's display label looked up from the country code, falling back to the code, or blank.
The Consignor row shows the consignor's name, or blank.
Arrival, Date created and Date submitted show dates as day, short month and year (for example 9 Oct 2026), and blank when missing or invalid.
The Arrival row shows only the arrival date, not the arrival time.
The Status row shows a GOV.UK tag: Draft (blue), Submitted (green), Amending (yellow) or Deleted (grey).
claims.note: Labels and colours live in shared copy and kit.js; the dashboard reuses them through journeyStrip.

claims.statement: A red 'Late' tag (Welsh 'Hwyr') shows beside the status tag when the notification is marked late.
claims.quote:
{% if row.late %}
              {{ govukTag({ text: copy.statusLate, classes: "govuk-tag--red" }) }}

claims.statement: Whether a notification is late comes from a lateNotificationIndicator on the stored notification; the dashboard does not calculate lateness itself.
The rule for when a notification counts as late is not visible on the dashboard.
claims.note: Looked in the dashboard, its view model and notification-helper; the indicator is read, not derived. No dashboard fit test covers the Late tag.

claims.statement: Link actions (View, Resume, Cancel amendment, Delete) render in the summary card's header action list.
Because they sit in a summary card, link actions get the reference appended to their accessible name, for example 'Delete (REF)'.
claims.quote:
// The dashboard renders its notification actions inside a GOV.UK summary card,
// which appends the card title — the reference — to each action's accessible name.

claims.statement: POST actions (Amend) render as secondary buttons, each in its own form with a CSRF crumb, in an 'Actions' row (Welsh 'Camau gweithredu') at the foot of the card; the row appears only when the card has a POST action.
A POST action button carries visually hidden text 'notification REF' (Welsh 'hysbysiad REF'), so Amend's accessible name is 'Amend notification REF'.
A Draft notification's card offers Resume then Delete.
A Submitted notification's card offers View, Amend and Delete, in that order.
An Amending notification's card offers Resume, Cancel amendment and Delete, in that order.
A notification in any other status offers no actions.
Resume (Welsh 'Ailddechrau') is a link to the notification's task hub at /notifications/{journeyId}.
View (Welsh 'Gweld') is a link to the notification's check answers view at /notifications/{journeyId}/notification-view.
Amend (Welsh 'Diwygio') is a button that posts to /notifications/{journeyId}/amend.
Amending a submitted notification puts it into amendment and takes the user to its task hub; if the amend cannot start, the user goes back to the dashboard.
claims.quote:
const journey = await amendJourney(request, h, request.params.journeyId)
  return h.redirect(journey ? hubPath(journey.journeyId) : dashboardPath())

claims.statement: Amend starts straight from the dashboard button with no confirmation page.
claims.note: The handler redirects immediately with no intermediate view.

claims.statement: Cancel amendment (Welsh 'Canslo diwygiad') is a link to /notifications/{journeyId}/cancel-amend.
Delete is a link labelled 'Delete' to /notifications/{journeyId}/delete, offered on Draft, Submitted and Amending cards.
There is no 'Copy as new' action on the dashboard; it is parked with reuse of a previous consignment.

There is no Copy as new action: it is parked with

claims.statement: The delete success banner shows whenever the dashboard URL carries deleted=1, regardless of whether a delete just happened.
The dashboard renders with the 'display' content column width.
The delete confirmation page is at /notifications/{journeyId}/delete, with GET and POST routes.
The delete page's title and level-1 heading is 'Delete this notification?' (Welsh 'Dileu'r hysbysiad hwn?').
The delete page body says 'This cannot be undone.' (Welsh 'Ni ellir dadwneud hyn.').
The delete page has a red warning button 'Yes, delete notification' (Welsh 'Iawn, dileu'r hysbysiad') that submits the form.
The delete page has a secondary link-button 'No, return to dashboard' (Welsh 'Na, dychwelyd i'r dangosfwrdd') going to the dashboard.
The delete page's Back link goes to the dashboard.
The delete page asks no question with options and has no validation or error message; it is a confirm-or-return page.
claims.note: The template has only two buttons, no radios or inputs; the partition's covers expected a question, options and error message.

claims.statement: The delete form posts a CSRF crumb and a concurrency token.
Only Draft, Submitted and Amending notifications can be deleted; asking to delete one in any other status redirects to the dashboard.
claims.quote:
journey.status === state.DRAFT ||
  journey.status === state.SUBMITTED ||
  journey.status === state.AMEND

claims.statement: Both delete routes check that the notification belongs to the user's session before reading it, and redirect to the dashboard if not.
claims.quote:
// Both handlers therefore check ownership before the first read.
const owns = (request) => isKnownJourney(request, request.params.journeyId)
claims.note: Ownership is checked in this layer because the state read would otherwise adopt any loadable journey into the session.

claims.statement: Confirming delete soft-deletes the notification and redirects to the dashboard with deleted=1, which shows the success banner.
If the soft delete reports nothing deleted, the user goes back to the dashboard with no banner.
Delete is a soft delete: the record is kept with a Deleted status rather than removed.
If saving the delete fails, the delete page re-renders with a recoverable error and HTTP 500.
claims.note: The recoverable error message itself is rendered by the shared layout, outside this part.

Confirming cancel amendment discards the amendment, restores the submitted version and redirects to the check answers view with cancelled=1.
If the cancel restores nothing, the user goes to the dashboard.
If saving the cancellation fails, the cancel amendment page re-renders with a recoverable error and HTTP 500.
What the check answers view shows for cancelled=1 (for example a success banner) is not set in the cancel amendment feature.
